source.title: Lenders turn to cuts, AI as strong jobs point to rate hikes
source.description: Nonbank mortgage payroll estimates dropped to a low for 2026 ahead of broader employment gains last month, pointing to a persistent need to manage origination staffing with retail productivity initiatives that have not yet reduced costs but at least contained them. Processing Content Industry-specific data the Bureau of Labor Statistics released with a one-month lag for real-estate credit and loan brokers, when combined, show industry payrolls dropped to 265,100 in August, marking the lowest point since the seasonally-slow first quarter. The statistics, combined with October's strong jobs report signaling a likelihood rates won't immediately fall further , suggest the industry is reducing origination staffing but are able to do so gradually as artificial intelligence has helped boost the number of loans closers handle.
